task_name: no slice is born with the plan gate unless its own row asks for it

rubric.result: The objective promises two things and both are in the diff. (1) `gatesForType` stops appending `plan`: `plugin/scripts/gates.js` now reads `return TYPE_GATES[typeof type === 'string' ? type.trim() : ''] ?? []`, with the `[...typed, 'plan']` line gone. (2) 'a groom creates no `gate:plan`': the chain that produces a groom's labels is `groom.js#buildLabels` -> `gateLabels(gatesOf(slice).gates)` -> `gatesOf` -> `resolveGates(slice.type, slice.gate, slice.e2e)` -> `implied = [...gatesForType(type), ...derived]`, so with the default gone a Gate-less row resolves to `[]` and `gateLabels([])` returns `[GATE_LABEL_NONE]`. The first verification one-liner pins exactly that over `['', 'backend', 'ui', 'infra', undefined]`. The declared observability signal is carried by this production line and nothing else: the diff adds no log line, no counter and no field — the groom already prints the labels it creates, which is the reader `conventions/simplicity.md` asks to be named ('who reads this, and where?'), so no instrumentation was owed or added. Nothing the objective names is missing and nothing extra was implemented in production: `gates.js` is the only non-test, non-plan file in the diff.

The **TDD:** line names `it('it is implied in NO slice: a row that wants it writes it in its Gate column')` in `gate-plan.test.js` and states five assertions. The test in the diff is that test, phrase for phrase: `expect(gatesForType('backend')).toEqual([])`, `expect(gatesForType('')).toEqual([])`, `expect(gatesForType(undefined)).toEqual([])`, `expect(gatesForType('ui')).toEqual(['visual'])` and `expect(resolveGates('backend', 'plan').gates).toContain('plan')` — same inputs, same expected values, in the same order, plus the pre-existing `expect(Object.values(TYPE_GATES).flat()).not.toContain('plan')` the file already carried. Nothing is asserted more loosely than the plan wrote it (`toEqual` where the plan said 'equal', `toContain` where it said 'contains').

The `Contract (plugin/scripts/gates.js)` block declares `export function gatesForType(type)   // -> TYPE_GATES[trimmed type] ?? []`. The diff states exactly that, with the same exported name, the same single parameter and the same trimming of a non-string input (`typeof type === 'string' ? type.trim() : ''`). The block's second sentence — 'The comment above the `return` is replaced by one recording D-14: no `Tipo` implies `plan`, a row that wants it writes `plan` in its `Gate` column, and the go protocol behind it is retired in later work (debt A-3)' — is honoured line by line by the new comment, which names D-14, names the six go modules as debt A-3 and points at `resolveGates` as the path a declaring row already has. `TYPE_GATES` (`ui: ['visual']`, `infra: ['apply']`), `resolveGates`, `resolveGatesForAgent`, `gateLabels`, `GATE_LABEL_NONE` and `parseGateCell` are untouched in the file as it stands. `GATES.plan` keeps BOTH texts byte for byte — I compared the `kickoff:` and `issue:` string literals in the diff against `plugin/scripts/gates.js:103-104` and only the explanatory comment above them changed, which is what the Contract block's own sentence about recording D-14 calls for.

The rows the diff bears on are D-14 and the two gate rows of the plan's table. D-14 retires the default and only the default: the diff removes `[...typed, 'plan']`, leaves `visual` and `apply` as the surviving Tipo gates in an untouched `TYPE_GATES`, and keeps `plan` in `GATES` with both texts, so `resolveGates('backend', 'plan').gates` still contains it — asserted in the TDD test and in the second verification one-liner. 'The protocol behind the go is **not** retired in this epic': `ct-go.mjs`, `ct-watch-go.mjs`, `go-channel.js`, `go-registry.js`, `go-response.js` and `dispatch-check.mjs` appear in neither `## Files changed` nor `## Rutas tocadas`, and `f38-the-plan-gate-go.test.js` — the suite that owns the exit-9 ladder — changed only its header comment, with its fixtures (`FAKE_GH_VIEW_LABELS: ['status:in-progress', 'gate:plan']`) already declaring the gate explicitly, so the new comment's claim about them is true. Row 'What `gatesForType` becomes | `return typed`': the diff returns the lookup expression directly instead of keeping the `typed` local; the value is identical and it is literally what the same brief's Contract block writes, so the row is implemented, not reopened. Row 'What happens to `!plan` in a row | it becomes an inert waiver … no code is added to silence it': no code was added; `resolveGates` classifies it through the untouched `inertWaivers` branch and the test asserts it. D-11 ('a yardstick is imported from the plugin, never reimplemented') is the row the reverted attempt would have broken, and it is honoured: the backend still reaches `gatesOf`/`gateLabels` through the plugin and grows no second opinion of its own.

Exemplar: `plugin/__tests__/f21-gate-and-type.test.js` is named as 'the suite that owns `TYPE_GATES` and `gatesForType`', and the diff edits it in its own idiom — exact `toEqual` over the resolved array, and the why recorded in the comment beside each corrected expectation. Rules: `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` (every new comment and test name in the diff is English; the Spanish that remains is the untouched `GATES.plan.kickoff` literal, which the plan protects); `backend/conventions/this-repository.md` is unengaged because the diff carries no backend production change. ct's yardstick, document by document: `style.md` — the file is the repository's declared debt for prose (an essay above every export) and CLAUDE.md keeps the no-prose and no-free-function exemptions here while refusing only the language one, so the seven-line comment added to `gatesForType` follows its host and the exemption is not being used to smuggle in a new concept — no new symbol is created anywhere in the diff. `simplicity.md` — the diff only removes; nothing is added with no caller, and 'observability answers to a reader who exists' is satisfied by adding no trace at all (the groom's existing `new labels … in <repo>` line and the `--dry-run` plan's `issues[].labels` are the readers the signal already had). `decisions.md` — the 'no Tipo implies plan' decision now lives in exactly one place, `gatesForType`; the change touched one file for the program to stay coherent, which is the yardstick's own test. `architecture.md`/`domain.md`/`boundaries.md` — no layer, port, adapter or boundary moves: `gates.js` is the plugin's pure vocabulary module and the backend keeps importing it rather than restating it. `testing.md` — the corrected tests keep asserting the observable effect (the resolved array, the labels a groom emits, the literal `gh` argv) and no arrange is built with the piece under test. `defects.md`, its four rules answered one by one: (1) closed vocabulary — subject present, and it holds: the gates stay members of the closed `GATES`/`GATE_ORDER` vocabulary, no boolean or loose string replaces them, no catch-all dispatch is introduced, and the absent case keeps being a declared member (`gateLabels([])` still returns `GATE_LABEL_NONE`) rather than an optional or a silence; (2) raw map as the return value of logic — `gatesForType` returns an array of vocabulary members; `TYPE_GATES` is a pre-existing constant catalogue read by key inside its own module and is untouched, so no new instance; (3) two fields that have to agree — subject present in the pre-existing `{gates, gatesDeclared}` pair and in `gate:none`, and the diff introduces neither a new pair nor a new sentinel: `gate:none` is the vocabulary's positive statement of absence, which is the opposite of an empty string standing for 'no message'; (4) an error named for where it happens — no subject: the diff adds, renames and removes no error. One residue, declared rather than reported as a finding because the plan's `### Out of scope` forbids the only fix: `GATES.plan.kickoff` still opens with '(implicado por defecto en TODO slice, salvo renuncia `!plan` en el spec)', which stopped being true with this diff, and the same section states '`GATES.plan` itself stays in the vocabulary with both its texts'. Both cannot be satisfied at once; the text now only ever reaches an agent whose row declared `Gate: plan`, where stopping is still correct.

Every `-` line in a test file was traced to a sentence of the task. The two removals the brief names verbatim are the two that happened: `it('it is implied in EVERY slice, whatever the Type may be — without touching TYPE_GATES')` and `it('`!plan` is a real per-row waiver: it removes the gate and makes noise like every waiver')` leave `gate-plan.test.js`, replaced by the two the **Tests:** line names. Everything else is an expectation corrected to the value the objective makes true, never an assertion dropped: each `-` has a `+` of the same or greater strength — `toEqual(['visual','plan'])` -> `toEqual(['visual'])`, `toContain('gate:plan')` -> `toContain(GATE_LABEL_NONE)` beside the surviving `not.toContain('gate:visual')`, and the f21 case that flipped gained an assertion (`buildLabels({...bareBackend, gate: 'plan'})` still contains `gate:plan`) instead of losing one. Two rewrites keep an assertion alive by changing the input rather than weakening the expectation: `e2e-resolution.test.js`'s 'e2e goes LAST in the canonical order' now feeds `resolveGates('ui', 'apply, plan', 'un recorrido')` so the four-gate ordering is still pinned, and `kickoff.test.js`'s 'a slice that keeps the `plan` gate…' declares `gates: ['plan'], gatesDeclared: true`, which the **Tests:** line authorises word for word ('whose slice now declares `gates: ['plan'], gatesDeclared: true`'), with its negative control untouched. `plan-issue-body.test.ts`'s gates-section test went from one assertion to two (`toContain('- (none) — …')` and `not.toContain('-OK <nonce>')`), and `gh-plan-issues.test.ts` changed only the literal label inside fixtures and expected argv, keeping every `expect` and every count. No test, case or assertion ended up asserting less.

The behaviour the objective promises is produced by production code and by nothing in the tests' scaffolding: `plugin/scripts/gates.js#gatesForType` is the single line that changed, and the two verification one-liners exercise it through `resolveGates`/`gateLabels` with no test file loaded at all. The plugin suites that changed drive the real `ct-groom.mjs`/`groom.js` (spawned, or `buildLabels`/`groomPlan` imported), and the backend suites drive the real `PlanIssueBody.labels`, which is `[...gateLabels(gatesOf(PlanIssueBody.rowFor({story, comment})).gates), GhPlanIssues.READY_LABEL]` over a row with `type: ''` and no `gate` key — so `gate:none` is computed by production, not hard-coded by the test. Revert `gates.js` and the new assertions fail; no expectation in this diff stands on a mock's return value.

Inside the declared files the diff writes only what the task asks: one production line and its comment in `gates.js`, and expectation corrections in fifteen test files. `### Out of scope` is respected name by name — no go-protocol module is touched, `GATES.plan` keeps both texts, and nothing of the review-plan, implement-plan or cmux work of the other tasks appears here. The plan hunk is an amendment and I read it line by line: it replaces the `**Files:**` line, adding seven plugin test files, two backend test files and the reason ('cannot stay green without correcting it alongside `gates.js` itself'), and it adds two paragraphs recording the reverted first attempt and a transient red. It REMOVES nothing: the old `**Files:**` routes are all still there, and `**TDD:**`, `**Tests:**`, the `Current state`/`Contract` blocks and the three `**Verification:**` commands are unchanged by the hunk. The added paths are justified: each named file asserted `gate:plan` as the value the retired default produced, which the objective makes false — I confirmed the mechanism for the two backend ones by reading production (`PlanIssueBody.labels` feeds `#sowing({ ours })`, so `gate:none` is both the label created and the one the retry ladder recognises as ours), and `backend/src/infrastructure/gh-plan-issues.ts` is genuinely absent from the diff, with `PlanIssueRow` carrying no `gate` field and `rowFor()` setting none — the retired default was not moved one layer down. One low finding on the amendment's one gap: it widened the files into `backend/__tests__/` without widening this task's own verification, which stays plugin-only.

The new tests are the two rewritten cases in `gate-plan.test.js` plus the renamed pair in `plan-issue-body.test.ts` and the `+` assertions inside the corrected suites. Deterministic: they call pure functions (`gatesForType`, `resolveGates`, `parseGateCell`, `buildLabels`, `PlanIssueBody.of`) or spawn `ct-groom.mjs` against a fixture spec with a faked `gh`; no clock, no date, no network, no randomness, no sleep. Isolated: the spawning suites build their own tree with `makeSpecDir`/`newRepoRoot` and `rmSync` it, the pure ones hold no state, and none depends on the order of the file. Verifies real behaviour: every new assertion is on what production returns — `expect(gatesForType('backend')).toEqual([])` and `expect(resolveGates('backend', 'plan').gates).toContain('plan')` both go red if this diff's `gates.js` line is reverted, and `expect(body).toContain('- (none) — this slice demands no human gate before merging.')` is the literal `renderGatesIssueContent` emits. I loaded `control-tower-loop:test-driven-development` before looking for anything beyond those three and found nothing to pin to it or to `testing-anti-patterns.md`: the names are sentences saying what is guaranteed ('it is implied in NO slice: a row that wants it writes it in its Gate column', 'the_gates_section_says_no_gate_is_asked_for_since_nothing_here_asks_for_one'), each covers one behaviour, and no assertion is on a mock's call count.

findings.what: The amendment adds two backend test files to `**Files:**` but leaves this task's `**Verification:**` as the two `node` one-liners plus `npm --prefix plugin test`, so the task's own gate never ran the suite it edits — `task-7-controls-2.log` ends at `npm --prefix plugin test` (149 files, 4033 tests) and contains no `npm --prefix backend test`. The two backend edits are in fact correct (I checked by reading: `PlanIssueBody.labels` is `[...gateLabels(gatesOf(PlanIssueBody.rowFor(...)).gates), READY_LABEL]` over a row with `type: ''` and no `gate`, which now yields `['gate:none','status:ready']`, and `open()` passes that same list as `ours` to `#sowing`, so every retry fixture that swapped `gate:plan` for `gate:none` still exercises the mechanism it names), and §8's global verification does run `npm --prefix backend test` for the slice — which is why this is a low and not more. What it costs is that an amendment which widened its files did not widen the control that measures them.
findings.evidence: "**Files:** ... `backend/__tests__/infrastructure/gh-plan-issues.test.ts` (modify), `backend/__tests__/infrastructure/plan-issue-body.test.ts` (modify)" — while the same task's **Verification:** block still reads only the two `node --input-type=module -e` one-liners and `npm --prefix plugin test`.
